title: CapturePack manifest.json
description: Schema for manifest.json, the REQUIRED entry point of a CapturePack, including capture-kind semantics defined through format 0.3.0 and backward compatibility with existing manifests that omit capture_kind (including early 0.3.0 RC output). It identifies the pack, records the capture environment, and inventories the variable parts of the pack (media and plugin payloads). Unknown additional properties are deliberately allowed everywhere: readers MUST accept unknown optional fields for forward compatibility (SPEC.md §13). See SPEC.md §5 for the normative definition; where schema and prose disagree, the prose wins.

format.description: Format marker. MUST be the literal string "capturepack". The first thing a reader checks to identify the file.

format_version.description: Oldest version of the CapturePack specification that fully expresses this pack, as semver (for example "0.1.0" or "0.3.0"). capture_kind was introduced in 0.3.0. Major (pre-1.0: minor) version changes are breaking; see SPEC.md §13.

capture_kind.description: What the user explicitly asked to capture, independent of recorder success: "video" for the recording workflow or "image" for the still-image workflow. New writers MUST include it and MUST declare format_version 0.3.0 or later. Readers and validators accept existing manifests where it is absent, including early 0.3.0 RC output; a replay filename then establishes video evidence, while replay:null alone does not distinguish an explicit still from a failed video.

id.description: RFC 4122 UUID uniquely identifying this pack. Version 4 (random) RECOMMENDED, lowercase RECOMMENDED.

created_at.description: Capture instant as ISO 8601 date-time. A timezone designator (offset or 'Z') MUST be present — local wall-clock time is context. Example: "2026-07-27T14:03:21+09:00".

generator.description: The software that wrote this pack.

name.description: Name of the generating tool, e.g. "capturepack".

version.description: Version of the generating tool. Note: this is the tool's version, not the format version.

title.description: OPTIONAL short human-readable title, one line. Used as the report.md heading and recommended as the basis of the pack filename.

note.description: OPTIONAL user-written intent, verbatim: what the user was doing, what they expected, what went wrong. Carried into report.md unchanged. The single most valuable field for an LLM reading the pack.

environment.description: Where the capture happened. Describes the hardware/OS environment; it does not define the annotation coordinate space (annotations are always in snapshot pixel coordinates, SPEC.md §8.2).

os.description: Operating system family, lowercase. Recommended values: "windows", "macos", "linux". Other values allowed for other platforms.

os_version.description: OPTIONAL (recommended) free-form OS version, e.g. "11 Pro 26200" or "14.5".

screens.description: OPTIONAL (recommended) list of displays present at capture time, in OS enumeration order.

scale.description: OS display scale factor (1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, ...). Default 1 when absent.

app.description: OPTIONAL name of the application that had focus at capture time, e.g. "notably.exe" or "Google Chrome". Plugins can attach richer window/app data under plugins/.

media.description: Declares the pack's media files. Readers MUST take the replay filename from media.replay rather than probing the pack for files.

snapshot.description: Filename of the snapshot image. In format 0.1.0 this MUST be "snapshot.png". Declared explicitly so future format versions can vary it without breaking readers that trust the manifest.

replay.description: Filename of the replay video — "replay.webm" (recommended; MediaRecorder output, no extra dependencies) or "replay.mp4" — or null when no replay was persisted. capture_kind records whether that null belongs to an explicit image capture or a video workflow without a saved recording. A pack contains at most one replay file.

image_scope.description: REQUIRED when capture_kind is "image". "region" means snapshot.png contains only the pixels inside crop_bounds. "fullscreen" means the user explicitly requested the complete virtual desktop and snapshot.png is one lossless composition containing every attached display, with no separate per-display raster. MUST be absent whenever capture_kind is not "image", including legacy manifests.

crop_bounds.description: REQUIRED for a region image and forbidden otherwise. Places the selected rectangle in the OS virtual-desktop device-independent-pixel space without storing any pixels outside it. Negative x/y are valid for monitors left of or above the primary display.

replay_duration_ms.description: Duration of the replay video in milliseconds. REQUIRED (as an integer) when replay is a filename; MUST be null or absent when replay is null.

replay_annotated.description: OPTIONAL filename of the annotated replay — "replay_annotated.webm" or "replay_annotated.mp4" — the replay with annotation boxes (blur, border, number badge, text) rendered into the pixels, playable in any player and always regenerable from replay + annotations.json (SPEC.md §7.2). MUST be absent when replay is null (nothing to render it from), and absent while the annotated replay has not (yet) been rendered. Writers MUST finish the file before publishing this declaration. Defensive readers that encounter a declared but missing file in an interrupted or older pack SHOULD treat the derived view as unavailable and fall back to replay + annotations.json.

snapshot_t_ms.description: OPTIONAL position in the replay timeline, in milliseconds, of the frame shown in snapshot.png — the same clock as timeline t_ms offsets relative to t0 (SPEC.md §10.1). Absent means the snapshot is the capture instant (the native 'now' frame). SHOULD be absent when replay is null: without a replay there is no timeline to anchor the value to. See SPEC.md §7.1 (frame-accurate captures).

trim_offset_ms.description: OPTIONAL, provenance only: when the writer trimmed the replay before saving, the position (ms) in the original captured recording of this replay's first frame (the trim in-point). Every time in the pack — annotation lifetimes, snapshot_t_ms, timeline offsets against t0 — is already on the trimmed replay's clock, so readers never apply this offset. Absent means the replay was never trimmed. SHOULD be absent when replay is null (SPEC.md §5.3). In a multi-display pack, every declared per-display replay SHOULD be cut to the same observed real-time interval; a shorter secondary buffer stays honestly shorter (SPEC.md §5.6).

displays.description: OPTIONAL per-display media of a capture that froze MORE THAN ONE display at the same instant (SPEC.md §5.6). Absent for a single-display capture. Exactly one entry has focused: true — the display whose media IS the top-level media, and the display a box without an explicit annotation.display belongs to — and that entry repeats the top-level media (snapshot "snapshot.png", the same replay filename and duration) rather than duplicating the bytes under a per-display name, so a reader that ignores this array still sees the whole pack. EVERY display can carry annotations (SPEC.md §8.8): a box names its screen in annotations.json's display field, its bounds are pixels in THAT display's snapshot, and a display that carries boxes gets its own rendered views here (replay_annotated / keyframes below). Every declared file must exist in the pack; index values are 1-based positions in environment.screens and must be unique.

index.description: 1-based position of this display in environment.screens (OS enumeration order). Unique within the array.

snapshot.description: Filename of this display's frozen frame: "snapshot-d<index>.png", except the focused entry, which repeats the top-level media.snapshot ("snapshot.png").

replay.description: Filename of this display's replay — "replay-d<index>.webm" (or .mp4), the top-level media.replay on the focused entry — or null when this display has no replay.

replay_duration_ms.description: Duration of this display's replay in milliseconds. REQUIRED when this entry's replay is a filename.

replay_clock_offset_ms.description: OPTIONAL measured conversion from the pack/focused replay clock to this display's replay clock, in integer milliseconds: display_t = pack_t + replay_clock_offset_ms. MUST be 0 on the focused entry and MUST be absent when replay is null. Legacy entries omit it and readers fall back to replay_duration_ms - top-level replay_duration_ms (SPEC.md §5.6).

replay_annotated.description: OPTIONAL: this display's replay with ITS OWN annotation boxes rendered into the pixels, "replay_annotated-d<index>.webm" (or .mp4) — SPEC.md §5.6, §7.2. Absent on the focused entry, whose annotated replay is the top-level media.replay_annotated, and absent on any display that carries no annotations or no replay. It contains ONLY the boxes whose display is this one: the same coordinates mean something different on every screen. A generated view, regenerable from this display's replay + annotations.json.

keyframes.description: OPTIONAL: this display's annotated stills, under "frames-d<index>/" — same shape and rules as the top-level media.keyframes (SPEC.md §5.7), containing only this display's boxes. t_ms is on THIS display's own replay clock, not the pack clock (the two are aligned by the rule in SPEC.md §5.6). Absent on the focused entry, whose stills are the top-level media.keyframes, and on any display without annotations.

file.description: Pack-relative filename "frames-d<index>/frame-<NN>_<MM-SS.mmm>.png", with the same NN and clock rules as the top-level keyframes.

t_ms.description: Position on THIS display's replay clock, in milliseconds, of the frame this still shows.

bounds.description: This display's rectangle in the OS virtual-desktop coordinate space, in device-independent pixels. Multiply by scale for physical pixels: bounds.width * scale equals the per-display snapshot's pixel width and environment.screens[index-1].width. The offsets place the screens relative to each other, which is what lets a viewer lay them out in their real arrangement.

x.description: Left edge in the virtual-desktop space (may be negative).

y.description: Top edge in the virtual-desktop space (may be negative).

focused.description: True on exactly one entry: the display whose media IS the top-level media, and the display a box with no explicit annotation.display belongs to.

replay_clock_offset_ms.description: A display without a replay has no replay clock; the offset MUST be absent.

keyframes.description: OPTIONAL annotated keyframe stills under frames/ (SPEC.md §5.7, §7.3): one PNG per annotation state change, with the annotations rendered into the pixels exactly as the annotated replay draws them — so a reader that cannot decode video still gets the whole story. Ordered by t_ms ascending; the NN in each filename is the entry's 1-based position. Written by the same background render as replay_annotated and declared with it, so the field is absent until that render completes (and in a pack that was never rendered). A screenshot-only pack has exactly one entry, t_ms 0, drawn from snapshot.png. Every declared file must exist in the pack; keyframes are a generated view, regenerable from the media + annotations.json, and never authoritative over annotations.json.

file.description: Pack-relative filename "frames/frame-<NN>_<MM-SS.mmm>.png": NN is this entry's 1-based position in the array (zero-padded to at least two digits) and MM-SS.mmm encodes t_ms, minutes zero-padded to at least two digits ('-' because ':' is not a legal filename character on Windows).

t_ms.description: Position on the replay clock, in milliseconds, of the frame this still shows — the same clock as annotation lifetimes, snapshot_t_ms and timeline offsets against t0. 0 in a screenshot-only pack.

replay_duration_ms.description: When a replay file is declared, its duration in milliseconds is required and must be an integer.
When replay is null (screenshot-only pack), replay_duration_ms must be null if present.

replay_annotated.description: When replay is null there is nothing to render an annotated replay from — replay_annotated MUST be absent (SPEC.md §5.3).

plugins.description: OPTIONAL inventory of plugin payload directories under plugins/. Absent or empty means no plugin data. Every plugin directory written by the exporter must have an entry here; readers MUST ignore plugin directories they do not recognize (SPEC.md §11).

name.description: Plugin name: lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens; no leading/trailing hyphen. Must equal the directory name under plugins/ and the name in that directory's meta.json.

version.description: Plugin version (semver recommended). Must equal the version in the plugin's meta.json.

path.description: Directory path relative to the pack root, with trailing slash. Must be exactly "plugins/<name>/" where <name> is this entry's name field (equality with name cannot be expressed in JSON Schema; see SPEC.md §5.4).
